whiteNoise.title: White Noise Generator
whiteNoise.description: Choose from 6 synthesized sounds and set the volume and stop timer. Save your favorite settings in this browser.

typeDesc.white: Noise with an even distribution across a broad frequency range.
typeDesc.pink: Noise with more low-frequency energy than white noise.
typeDesc.brown: A deeper noise with a stronger emphasis on low frequencies.
typeDesc.rain: Synthesized rain made from filtered noise and short variations.
typeDesc.wind: Synthesized wind with a slowly changing sound level.
typeDesc.wave: Synthesized waves that grow and fade in a repeating rhythm.

benefits.title: What this tool does
items: Choose and play one of 6 synthesized sounds.
Adjust volume from 0 to 100 and set a stop timer.
Use a final 30-second fade-out and save up to 6 settings.
Sound and settings are handled within this browser.

tips.title: Things to know
items: No sound starts until you press Play.
The volume number is not a measurement of your device's actual sound level.
Selecting a different timer starts that duration from the moment you change it.
Loading settings stops the sound. Press Play when you want to listen again.

whatIs.title: What is the White Noise Generator?
whatIs.description: Generate six synthesized sounds in the browser and adjust volume, a deadline timer, and an optional fade. Save up to six named settings and load them explicitly. Loading a setting or returning to the page does not automatically play audio.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Choose a sound and volume. Volume 0 means muted, which is different from stopping playback.
2. Choose no timer or 5, 10, 15, 30, or 60 minutes, and optionally enable the final 30-second fade.
3. Press play. Changing the timer during playback restarts its deadline from now; changing sound or volume keeps the deadline.
4. Save frequent combinations by name. Loading stops the existing sound and applies settings only, so press play again yourself.

items.q: Does an expired timer start playing again when I return?
items.a: Audio is not resumed after its deadline. A rejected play or resume attempt is not shown as successful. Exact background execution during OS app suspension or device sleep is not guaranteed.

items.q: What is stored in a saved setting?
items.a: Up to six settings store a name of at most 40 characters, sound, volume, timer, and fade. Playback state, remaining time, and audio buffers are not saved. Loading applies settings without automatically playing.

items.q: How do the timer and fade work?
items.a: A timer sets a deadline for the chosen minutes from now. Sound or volume changes keep that deadline. The optional final 30-second fade is off by default. No timer means indefinite playback.
